issues: React hydration warning in dev bundle: injected editor <span> inside <option> from static-imported UNITS array — appears to be Emergent editor instrumentation (x-source-var UNITS at Calendar.jsx line 9). Harmless in production build but noisy in dev. No visual impact; option text is readable.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1153 lines — still exceeds the 700-line guideline; splitting into modules (events/ical, calendar_feed, whiteboard_gallery, reminders_cron, markers, notebooks) would improve maintainability.

POST /api/whiteboard/gallery accepts unbounded base64 'image' strings — consider max-size guard and (optional) storing images as separate collection docs referenced by id to avoid Mongo 16MB doc caps for large canvases.

GET /api/ical/{token}.ics is public by design (needed for external clients) but leaks all family event titles. Consider a per-user ical token or a shared secret rotation UI; current implementation stores a single global token in db.settings.ical_token — no way to rotate/revoke from UI.

_process_reminders detects 'due <= now <= due+1h' — if the cron misses a full hour (deployment restart, network outage), reminders can be missed silently. Consider a 'past-due-window' catch-up or persistent 'next_due_at' index.
EventBody accepts arbitrary reminders payload (List[Dict]); consider a Pydantic sub-model {value:int>=0, unit:Literal['minutes','hours','days']} for validation.

PUT /events/{id} does not preserve reminders_sent — an edit resets sent state indirectly (since only body.model_dump is $set, but reminders_sent is not in EventBody, so it is left intact). Good — verified in code. No action.
Postcards marker color hard-coded to #10B981 in server; consistent with spec. Frontend list correctly omits user_name (verified in Playwright — no Admin/Mama in list under map).

No auth on GET /api/ical/{token}.ics is correct for iCal subscription, but currently ANY authenticated user (or with the leaked token) sees ALL events including personal ones — no per-user filtering. Acceptable for family-shared calendar but worth documenting.
